rep.angle: lead with a recent hiring push you noticed
rep.name: Dev

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Dev from HyperSale, I noticed BrightPath's recent sales hiring push can I take 30 seconds to explain why ramp consistency prompted my call?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hypersale lets new reps practice realistic buyer calls before prospects, while managers see quote-backed progress weekly, how are you keeping ramp quality consistent across hires?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already have Gong for this.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: �That makes sense� Gong is strong after the call, Hypersale adds practice before it, where are new hires rehearsing before live prospects today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: New hires practice on live prospects. Managers don't have time for another tool.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I hear you this should save manager time, not ad work, how many live prospect calls does each hire need before they're consistently ready?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: About a dozen calls, give or take. How would I even measure whether practice works?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: We compare pilot reps' time to consistency and first call quality against your dozen-call baseline. Every score cites the quote, How many hires this quarter?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We’ve got about 15 ramping this quarter. What's your pilot cost?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Annual pricing is $90 per rep monthly, pilot cost depends on team size, how many of the 15 would you want included?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I can sponsor under $15k. How many reps fit that?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: 13 reps cost $14,040 annually, all 15 cost $16,200, could we scope a 30 day pilot Tuesday at 2 with UN enablement?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: All right, let's do 13 reps. Tuesday at 2 works. I've got a meeting, I need to go.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Perfect I'll send Tuesday at 2 with you and enablement to scope the 13 rep pilot.
